title: Type attribute region
brief: Five concrete attribute regions for the same EstimatePairOut Type. Every direction starts compact, can reveal nested shape information, and keeps Python-like type annotations editable on the canvas.
defaultWhy: V1 makes ordinary text the one canonical authoring surface while the compact tree remains a projection. It is the only direction that makes cursor placement, Enter, multiline paste, and a nested ergonomic read all first-class without a second editable representation.
decisionHinge: If per-field structured editing becomes more important than whole-snippet paste and Python-shaped source, V3 becomes the better fit; it does not lose on visual density alone.
invariants: One canonical type body; Port and expanded views only project it.
No inference, validation, or hidden rewrite of author-written types.
Flat by default; nested detail is opt-in and reversible.
The representative content is EstimatePairOut with pose / quality and a nested Position.
boundary: Runnable UI specimens only. Parsing, persistence, shape integration, and the chevron placement preference are implemented separately in the product track.

requirements.name: Text-native authoring
requirements.why: The Type should accept a cursor anywhere, Enter, selection, and pasted annotations without translating the author into a form.
requirements.passCondition: A person can paste or edit a multi-line Python-shaped member declaration as one ordinary text operation.

anchors.1: Only individual cells can be edited.
anchors.3: A text view exists but interrupts the primary interaction.
anchors.5: The canvas itself provides one normal multiline editing transaction.

requirements.name: Compact typed reading
requirements.why: Early domain modeling needs a lot of type vocabulary visible without turning every type into a large class diagram.
requirements.passCondition: Two top-level attributes remain scannable at normal canvas scale while a nested pose can be opened in place.

anchors.1: Nested detail is always open or hard to find.
anchors.3: The tree is readable with repeated chrome.
anchors.5: The default is as compact as source text and expansion stays spatially stable.

requirements.name: One body, many views
requirements.why: A Type must not fork when shown as a compact signature, an expanded definition, or later as code.
requirements.passCondition: The proposal has one authored body and describes Port / expanded representations as read projections.

anchors.1: Each view has independent editable data.
anchors.3: A sync rule is needed to keep views aligned.
anchors.5: Only one body is editable; every other view is derived on demand.

requirements.name: Whiteboard fit
requirements.why: SystemSketch remains a permissive whiteboard beside Python, so the type surface must not become a miniature IDE or enforce correctness.
requirements.passCondition: Malformed or incomplete text stays visible and editable rather than being blocked or auto-corrected.

anchors.1: The editor rejects incomplete type text.
anchors.3: The UI tolerates text but adds a prominent error workflow.
anchors.5: Any text remains a literal board fact; parsing only changes the read projection.

hardGates.name: No competing editable bodies
hardGates.why: A result cannot win if Port, tree, or code view can drift from one another.

hardGates.name: Nested disclosure is visible
hardGates.why: A direction cannot win if opening a nested record requires leaving the Type context.

variants.name: Source-first tree
variants.thesis: Store one multiline attribute source; parse it only to paint the compact, foldable tree.
variants.bestWhen: You model in Python-shaped snippets and want the canvas to behave like a light text field.
variants.losesWhen: You need mouse-first per-field normalization, reordering, or generated forms.

decisions.label: Canonical body
decisions.value: A single `attributeSource` string on the Type Block.

decisions.label: Read view
decisions.value: A parsed tree with hover-only inline chevrons and a local gutter alternative.

decisions.label: Write view
decisions.value: Click any row to enter one normal multiline textarea; blur commits, Escape cancels.

proof: The specimen toggles from a compact tree to an editable multiline body.
Nested fields remain in the same spatial region when opened.

variants.name: Foldable code cell
variants.thesis: Treat the region as a miniature code editor with always-left gutter controls and syntax ink.
variants.bestWhen: The Type body should look and behave like a narrow source file and future Code Blocks share its editor.
variants.losesWhen: The visual form needs to feel like part of a whiteboard card rather than a code surface.

decisions.label: Disclosure

decisions.label: Tradeoff
decisions.value: Great text behavior, but an IDE grammar dominates a compact Type.

variants.name: Structured attribute table
variants.thesis: Persist attributes as fields and edit Name, Type, and Default in separate cells.
variants.bestWhen: You want column-level editing, row commands, sorting, or future schema-driven forms.
variants.losesWhen: Typing a complete annotation or pasting a record definition should remain one ordinary gesture.

variants.name: Direct outline editor
variants.thesis: Make the tree itself the editor: click a row, type in place, add child rows with outline commands.
variants.bestWhen: Mouse-first gradual disclosure matters more than a whole-snippet authoring workflow.
variants.losesWhen: People regularly paste NamedTuple fields or refactor text with normal code-editor movements.

decisions.label: Primary model
decisions.value: Tree nodes are authored records, not a parsed projection.

decisions.label: Interaction
decisions.value: Enter adds a sibling; Tab changes nesting; chevrons manage subtrees.

decisions.label: Tradeoff
decisions.value: Beautiful tree ergonomics, but it invents a second mini-language and keyboard contract.

variants.name: Compact card + inspector
variants.thesis: Keep only a one-line attributes signature on canvas and edit the full body in an inspector panel.
variants.bestWhen: The canvas must stay visually sparse and types are edited infrequently.
variants.losesWhen: Early modeling needs rapid type writing in the spatial context of transformations.
